title: Sell Stuff Around Your House for Cash: 30 Things + Apps
excerpt: The best things to sell to make money are already in your house, and the right app can turn clutter into $200–$500 fast.
quick_answer: The best things to sell to make money are already sitting in your house: electronics, brand-name clothes, furniture, kids' gear, and unused gift cards. Most people clear $200–$500 in a weekend using apps like Facebook Marketplace, Poshmark, and Decluttr. Start with high-value items first.
content:
When money's tight and payday is still a week away, the advice to "just make more money" feels almost insulting. You can't magic up a second job overnight, and cutting your budget only stretches so far. But here's something that actually helps fast: the best things to sell to make money aren't things you have to buy or produce. They're already in your closets, your garage, and that drawer full of old phones. Most homes are quietly sitting on hundreds of dollars in stuff you forgot you owned. Selling it won't fix everything, and this isn't about feeling ashamed of clutter. It's about turning what you already have into cash you can use this week for groceries, a bill, or breathing room. Let's go through exactly what sells, where to sell it, how to price it, and how to actually get paid without the process eating your whole weekend.

## What Are the Best Things to Sell for Quick Cash?

The best things to sell to make money are high-value, easy-to-ship, or in-demand items you no longer use. Electronics and brand-name goods bring the most per item, while clothes and kids' gear sell in volume. Start with anything worth $20 or more, since those sell fastest and pay best.

Here are 30 things hiding in most homes:

1. Old phones, tablets, and laptops
2. Video game consoles and games
3. Brand-name clothing and shoes
4. Handbags and designer accessories
5. Furniture (dressers, tables, couches)
6. Kids' clothes, toys, and gear
7. Baby items (strollers, carriers, cribs)
8. Power tools and yard equipment
9. Kitchen appliances and small gadgets
10. Jewelry and watches
11. Books, textbooks, and vinyl records
12. Exercise equipment
13. Unused gift cards
14. Cameras and lenses
15. Home decor and lamps

Add bikes, holiday decor, board games, craft supplies, and unopened beauty products, and most families easily reach 30 sellable items. Sort them into two piles: worth over $20 and worth under $20. The high-value pile is your priority.

## Which Apps Pay the Most for Your Stuff?

Different apps pay best for different items, so matching the item to the platform is how you earn the most. Furniture sells fast locally on Facebook Marketplace, clothes do best on Poshmark, and electronics get instant offers on Decluttr. Using the right one can double what you'd get elsewhere.

Here's a quick match-up:

- **Facebook Marketplace:** furniture, appliances, tools, anything bulky. Free, local, fast, no shipping.
- **Poshmark & Mercari:** clothing, shoes, accessories, home goods. Built-in buyers, easy shipping.
- **eBay:** electronics, collectibles, rare items. Widest audience, higher fees.
- **Decluttr:** phones, tech, CDs, DVDs. Instant quote, they pay you directly.
- **OfferUp:** local sales similar to Marketplace.

If you have a closet full of clothes, our guide to the [cash envelope system](/blog/cash-envelope-system-beginners) pairs nicely with reselling, because you can drop your earnings straight into an envelope goal. For big or heavy items, always sell locally to skip shipping costs and hassle. For small, valuable, mail-friendly items, shipping apps reach far more buyers. Pick two apps to start, not all six, so you don't spread yourself thin.

## How Do You Price Items So They Actually Sell?

Price used items at 30–50% of what they cost new, then adjust based on condition and demand. Buyers on resale apps expect a deal, so pricing too high just means your item sits for weeks. A fair price that sells this weekend beats a dream price that never does.

A simple pricing method:

1. Search the app for your exact item to see what similar ones sold for (not just listed for)
2. Price at the middle of that sold range
3. Add 10–15% wiggle room so you can accept an offer and still feel good
4. Note the condition honestly in the title ("like new," "gently used")

Great photos matter more than most people think. Use daylight near a window, a clean background, and take five or six angles including any flaws. Clear photos and an honest description cut down on lowball offers and no-shows. Say a jacket cost $80 new: list it around $32, accept $28, and it's gone by Sunday. If something hasn't sold in two weeks, drop the price 15%. Momentum matters more than squeezing out an extra $5 that keeps the clutter in your house.

## How Can You Turn Selling Into a Repeatable Money Habit?

Selling becomes reliable income when you treat it as a small routine instead of a one-time purge. People who declutter for cash regularly can add $100–$300 a month to their household, which is real breathing room when you're living paycheck to paycheck. The key is a simple system you'll actually keep.

Try this monthly rhythm:

- Keep a "sell box" in a closet; add items you stop using all month
- Set one hour every other weekend to list and ship
- Reinvest a small amount in restocking things you can flip (more on that in our thrift-flipping guide)
- Move every dollar earned into a named goal, not general spending

Directing your earnings on purpose is what makes the effort feel worth it. On $200 a month, that's $2,400 a year, enough to fully fund a starter emergency cushion. Sending each sale straight into an [emergency fund](/blog/emergency-fund) or a specific bill turns random cash into visible progress. Some people funnel selling income into a debt payment; others build a small buffer. Whatever you choose, name the goal before the money lands, so it doesn't quietly vanish into everyday spending and leave you wondering where it went.

## What Mistakes Cost Sellers the Most Money?

The biggest mistake sellers make is giving up on high-value items too early or pricing everything at once and getting overwhelmed. Rushed, disorganized selling leaves real money on the table. A little patience and a few safety habits protect both your earnings and your peace of mind.

Avoid these common slip-ups:

- **Blurry or dark photos** that make good items look worthless
- **Vague titles** that don't include the brand, size, or model buyers search for
- **Meeting strangers unsafely:** always meet in a public spot or a police-station "safe exchange" zone
- **Accepting sketchy payment:** use the app's built-in payment or cash in person; never wire money or ship before you're paid
- **Trashing "junk":** broken electronics and single shoes can still sell for parts or crafts

One more: don't let listings pile up unanswered. Buyers move fast, and replying within a few hours often decides the sale. Keep your process light and safe, and selling stays a steady, low-stress way to turn what you already own into cash you can use right now.

## How Do You Sell the Big, Bulky Stuff Without the Hassle?

Big items like couches, dressers, and treadmills hold the most cash but scare people off because of moving and meetups. The fix is simple: sell them locally, price them to move, and make the buyer do the heavy lifting. A $500 couch you never listed is $500 sitting in your living room.

Handle bulky sales the easy way:

1. **List local only** on Facebook Marketplace or OfferUp - never ship furniture
2. **Write "buyer must pick up"** clearly in the description
3. **Photograph it clean and staged,** in good daylight, from three angles
4. **Price 40–50% of new** so it sells in days, not months
5. **Meet in your driveway or garage,** never inside your home, and have someone with you

Set a firm pickup window so tire-kickers don't waste your Saturday. Ask for the app's payment or cash on pickup, counted before the item leaves. One dresser at $60 and a couch at $150 can cover a whole grocery week. Big items feel like the most work, but they pay the most per hour of effort by far.
seo_title: Sell Stuff Around Your House for Cash: 30 Things + Apps
seo_description: Discover the best things to sell to make money from home. 30 items hiding in your house plus the top apps to turn clutter into $200–$500 fast.

faq_items.question: What sells the fastest for cash?
faq_items.answer: Furniture, electronics, and brand-name items sell fastest because demand is high and buyers are always searching for them. Locally, a well-priced dresser or couch on Facebook Marketplace can sell within a day. For mail-in items, phones and tablets get near-instant offers on Decluttr, so you can turn tech into cash the same week.

faq_items.question: How much money can I realistically make selling my stuff?
faq_items.answer: Most households clear $200–$500 in a focused weekend of decluttering, and $100–$300 a month if they keep at it. Your total depends on what you own: homes with electronics, tools, and brand-name clothing earn more. Start with items worth over $20, since those bring the biggest return for your time.

faq_items.question: Is it safe to sell things to strangers online?
faq_items.answer: Yes, when you take basic precautions. Always meet local buyers in a public place or a police-station safe-exchange zone, bring someone with you, and only accept cash or the app's built-in payment. Never ship an item before you're paid, and never wire money. These simple habits prevent nearly all scams.

faq_items.question: Do I have to pay taxes on things I sell around my house?
faq_items.answer: Usually not, if you're selling personal items for less than you originally paid. That's considered decluttering, not income. If you start flipping items for profit regularly, that can become taxable. When in doubt, keep simple records of what you sell and check current IRS guidelines or a tax professional.

faq_items.question: Which app is best for a total beginner?
faq_items.answer: Facebook Marketplace is the easiest starting point. It's free, most people already have an account, there's no shipping to learn, and buyers are local. List a few clear photos, price fairly, and arrange a public meetup. Once you're comfortable, add Poshmark for clothes or Decluttr for electronics.

faq_items.question: How do I get more buyers to actually respond to my listings?
faq_items.answer: Respond fast, price fairly, and post clear daylight photos with the brand and model in the title. Buyers scroll quickly and message several sellers at once, so a reply within an hour often wins the sale. Relisting an unsold item after a week also bumps it back to the top of search results.
